title: Ice and Rain Protection — Wing Anti-Ice — Install the High Force Solenoid and Resolved Position Feedback

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Mandatory conversion of the wing anti-ice shut-off valves to the high force solenoid and resolved position feedback standard, following an airworthiness directive raised after repeated slow-open events in cold conditions.

sections.planning_reason: Sixty-two events were recorded across four winter seasons in which a wing anti-ice shut-off valve took long enough to open after a cold soak that the crew saw a fault indication. Investigation showed the solenoid pull-in force marginal against cold seal friction at minus forty degrees, and the single position switch declaring a failure before the valve completed travel. Two operators had adopted the practice of selecting anti-ice on the ground to avoid the indication, which is not an acceptable mitigation. The airworthiness authority issued a directive requiring conversion within a defined period.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives the instructions to replace the solenoid on each wing anti-ice shut-off valve with the high force item, and to replace the single position switch with the resolved feedback arrangement built around the new sensor assembly and non-return valve body. The mounting hardware and sealing washers are renewed. The valve connector wiring is re-terminated and the harness support in the leading edge is moved inboard so that the longer solenoid clears the piccolo duct flange. The bleed monitoring computer threshold that declares the valve failed is widened through the configuration procedure after the hardware change.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Depressurise the pneumatic system and make sure that the wing anti-ice is deselected and safetied. Open the leading edge access panels. Disconnect the valve connector and remove the existing solenoid and position switch. Install the high force solenoid, the sensor assembly and the non-return valve body, renewing the mounting hardware and the sealing washers. Move the harness support inboard to the position given in the installation drawing and re-clamp. Re-terminate the valve connector. Install the second wing in the same way. Restore pneumatic pressure and do the valve travel and timing check using AMM-T-30-10-11-400-001-A. Apply the widened overheat threshold through the bleed monitoring computer configuration procedure. Do the anti-ice functional test at ambient and record the travel times. Close the leading edge panels. Record the modification and update the configuration record.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to Auran powered TITAN-88 aircraft in the MSN T00001 to T00166 range, excluding MSN T00116 and MSN T00118 which were converted before delivery. CVX-7270 powered aircraft are covered by a separate bulletin and are outside this effectivity because the bleed pressure schedule differs.
sections.material_note: Kit K3010-1021-01 covers one aircraft, both wings. The sensor assembly is a twenty-eight week lead item. Revision 02 added the second wing kit as a separate orderable item after operators asked to convert one wing at a time during short layovers.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 30 months after the effective date of the associated airworthiness directive, or before the next winter operating season if the aircraft has recorded a slow-open event, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Second wing kit made separately orderable; travel time acceptance band corrected in step 9; effectivity clarified for aircraft converted before delivery
